messages.subject: SEM, Binary DV,  low CFI
parts:
I have a model with three latent variables (four, five, and eight indicators) as predictors and one binary outcome. I am using a DWLS estimator. Binary DV is a decision to donate or not in different ocasions. I have three different studies but the model is same across studies.

In one study, I have 450 participants who donated and 70 who did not. I read that a high difference in number of participants between categories in binary DV should not be a problem for SEM. However, I am wondering can this big difference cause low robust CFI?

Is it recommendable at all to use SEM if the number of participants in one of categories in binary DV is small (in my case only 70)? Should I maybe opt for path analysis or logistic regression?

In another two samples, the overall number of participants is low: 136:30 and 91:28 (donated:did not donate). I guess in this case it would be best to switch to path analysis or logistic regression?

Thank you!

Aneta

Thanks!

Aneta

messages.author: d240a1aabd16bc4c
messages.subject: Re: SEM, Binary DV, low CFI
parts:
Depends on the sample but

In the first sample (450:70): CFI = .787, RMSEA = .078 90% CI [0.071, 0.084], SRMR = .066

In the second sample (136:30): CFI = .702, RMSEA = .090 90% CI [0.077, 0.102], SRMR = .088.

In the third sample (91:28): CFI = .706, RMSEA = .076 90% CI [0.057, 0.093], SRMR = .087

In all sample chi square is significant.

In the first sample all model fit indices can be improved by removing one observed item. In other two samples whatever I do I cannot improve CFI.
